clips.linkedin:
Give your AI last quarter's paid campaigns and your list growth, and it shows which left you an audience you own.

Owned media is what you control, paid is what you buy and earned is what others choose to say about you. The useful question is how they feed each other.

Use paid and earned to grow owned. A paid campaign that builds the email list keeps paying off after the budget stops. Our view is that most brands under-invest in owned because its returns are slow, then overspend on paid to make up for an audience they never built.

So judge every paid campaign partly by the owned audience it leaves behind. Your AI can do that check and say plainly where the data can't connect the two.

The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/owned-paid-earned-media-basics/ (the podcast voices are AI-generated).
clips.text: Use paid and earned to grow owned. A paid campaign that builds the email list keeps paying off after the budget stops. Coverage that links to a genuinely useful page on your site brings readers you can keep. And good owned content, clear and well sourced, gives journalists and AI answers something to cite. So the loop runs both ways. And where do most brands get that wrong? Our view is that most brands under-invest in owned because its returns are slow, and then overspend on paid to make up for an audience they never built. So start any audit with owned, and judge every paid and earned activity partly by how much owned audience it leaves behind.

clips.linkedin:
Give your AI last quarter's paid campaigns and your list growth, and it shows which left you an audience you own.

Most media plans have a type doing no clear job, and most teams can't say which paid campaigns grew the audience they own.

Both are jobs for AI. Give it a list of every channel you use, with spend and results where you have them, and it sorts each into owned, paid, earned or rented, says what job each is doing, and flags any type with no clear job.

Then give it last quarter's paid campaigns and your list growth over the same weeks. It shows which campaigns left owned audience behind and which didn't, and says where the data can't connect the two.

The prompts are in the show notes, with the full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/owned-paid-earned-media-basics/ (the podcast voices are AI-generated).
clips.text: Get AI on this: the media audit itself. Give it a list of every channel you use, with spend and results where you have them, and it sorts each one into owned, paid, earned or rented, says what job each is doing, and flags any type with no clear job. Second, get AI on checking the hand-offs. Give it last quarter's paid campaigns and your list growth over the same weeks, and it shows which campaigns left owned audience behind and which didn't. It'll say plainly where the data can't connect the two.
